🥘 Ingredients

  • 4 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs, about 1.5 lbs
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • 1 teaspoon garlic powder
  • Salt and pepper to taste
  • 2 cups baby potatoes, halved
  • 1 cup baby carrots
  • 1 cup broccoli florets
  • 1 lemon, sliced
  • 2 sprigs fresh rosemary

👩‍🍳 Instructions

  1. Start by patting the chicken thighs dry with paper towels. This step is crucial because dry skin crisps up better in the air fryer. Then, rub the chicken all over with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, smoked paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. The oil helps the spices stick and promotes browning. Don’t skimp on seasoning here—it makes a huge difference in flavor. Let the chicken sit while you prep the veggies, giving the spices time to settle in.
  2. Toss the baby potatoes and carrots with the remaining tablespoon of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Make sure they are well coated to ensure even roasting. The potatoes and carrots take a bit longer to cook than the broccoli, so we'll add the broccoli later to avoid overcooking. Cutting potatoes in halves speeds up cooking and helps them get crispy edges.
  3. Arrange the seasoned chicken thighs skin-side up in the air fryer basket, leaving space between pieces for air circulation. Place the potatoes and carrots around the chicken. This setup allows the chicken fat to render and flavor the veggies. Adding lemon slices and rosemary sprigs on top infuses the dish with bright, herbal notes. The air fryer’s circulating hot air crisps the chicken skin while roasting the veggies underneath.
  4. Set the air fryer to 380°F (193°C) and cook for 15 minutes. This initial high heat jumpstarts the skin crisping and begins roasting the potatoes and carrots. Avoid opening the basket during this time to maintain consistent temperature and ensure even cooking. The smell will start to become irresistible!
  5. After 15 minutes, open the air fryer and add the broccoli florets around the chicken and other veggies. Broccoli cooks faster, so adding it later prevents it from becoming mushy. Give everything a gentle toss to mix flavors but keep the chicken skin facing up. This step balances the cooking times perfectly.
  6. Continue cooking for another 12-15 minutes at 380°F. The chicken should reach an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C) for safe consumption. The potatoes should be tender when pierced with a fork, and the broccoli bright green and slightly crispy on the edges. Resist the urge to overcook to keep everything juicy and flavorful.
  7. Once cooked, remove the chicken and veggies from the air fryer and let the chicken rest for 5 minutes. Resting allows the juices to redistribute inside the meat, making it more tender and juicy. Use this time to plate your meal or prepare a simple side salad if you like. Don’t skip resting—it really improves texture.
  8. Squeeze the roasted lemon slices over the chicken and veggies for a fresh citrusy finish. The caramelized lemon adds a subtle tang that cuts through the richness of the chicken skin. You can also sprinkle a little more fresh rosemary or parsley if you have it on hand. This simple finishing touch brightens the whole dish beautifully.
  9. Serve immediately while warm, pairing with your favorite grain or a crisp green salad. This one-pot meal is satisfying on its own but also versatile enough to complement other sides. Leftovers store well and reheat beautifully in the air fryer or oven, keeping that crispy skin intact.

🥘 Ingredients

  • 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, chilled
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 cup unsalted butter, cold and cubed
  • 3-4 tablespoons ice water
  • 4 large ripe tomatoes, sliced
  • 1 teaspoon salt, divided
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1/2 teaspoon dried basil
  • 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano
  • 1 cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese
  • 1/2 cup shredded mozzarella cheese
  • 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese
  • 2 tablespoons mayonnaise
  • 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard
  • Fresh basil leaves for garnish

👩‍🍳 Instructions

  1. Start by making the pie crust. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour and salt. Add the cold, cubed butter and use a pastry cutter or your fingers to blend it until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs with some pea-sized pieces. This texture is key for a flaky crust because the small lumps of butter create steam pockets as they bake. Be careful not to overwork the dough or the crust will turn tough. Slowly add ice water, one tablespoon at a time, mixing gently until the dough just comes together. Wrap it in plastic and chill for at least 30 minutes to relax the gluten and firm up the butter.
  2. While the dough chills, slice the tomatoes into about 1/4-inch thick rounds. Lay them out on paper towels or a cooling rack and sprinkle with half the salt. Let them sit for 20-30 minutes to draw out excess moisture. This step is crucial to avoid a soggy pie. After resting, gently pat the tomatoes dry to remove the released liquid. This technique keeps the crust crisp and the filling from becoming watery.
  3. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Roll out the chilled dough on a lightly floured surface into a 12-inch circle. Transfer it carefully to a 9-inch pie dish, pressing gently to fit and trimming any excess edges. Dock the bottom with a fork to prevent bubbling during baking. Blind bake the crust by lining it with parchment paper and filling with pie weights or dried beans. Bake for 15 minutes until the edges start to turn golden. This pre-baking step ensures the crust stays crisp once the filling is added.
  4. In a small bowl, mix together the mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, remaining salt, black pepper, dried basil, and oregano. This flavorful base adds creaminess and depth to the filling. Spread this mixture evenly over the partially baked crust. This layer acts as a moisture barrier and flavor enhancer, ensuring the cheese and tomatoes meld perfectly.
  5. Layer the tomato slices evenly over the mayo-mustard base, slightly overlapping them. Sprinkle the shredded cheddar and mozzarella cheeses over the tomatoes, then finish with a dusting of Parmesan. The combination of cheeses melts beautifully and adds a sharp, creamy contrast to the juicy tomatoes. Be generous but don’t overload to keep the pie balanced.
  6. Place the pie on the middle rack of the preheated oven and bake for 25-30 minutes. You’re looking for the cheese to melt completely and start bubbling with golden brown spots. The crust should be deep golden and crisp around the edges. Avoid opening the oven too often to maintain steady heat and even baking.
  7. Once baked, remove the pie from the oven and let it cool for at least 10 minutes before slicing. This resting time helps the filling set slightly so it doesn’t spill out when cut. It also allows the flavors to meld and the crust to crisp up a little more as it cools.
  8. Garnish with fresh basil leaves just before serving for a bright, herbal note that complements the rich cheese and tart tomatoes. The fresh basil adds an aromatic finish that elevates the whole dish.
  9. Serve the tomato pie warm or at room temperature. It pairs wonderfully with a simple green salad or a light soup for a complete meal. Leftovers reheat well and taste just as delicious the next day.
